Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: VeriFayda digital authentication system operational with over 32.3 million successful authentications by September 2025 (averaging 130,000 per day). Supports real-time biometric and demographic authentication. VeriFayda 2 (EthSwitch eKYC) launched with improved functionality.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Fayda mobile app (available via telebirr super app mini app) allows individuals to view their ID data, access digital copy of ID, and update demographic information. PDPP 2024 provides rights of access, rectification, and erasure. Consent-based data sharing framework operational.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: VeriFayda 1 and VeriFayda 2 eKYC systems fully operational. NBE mandated all banks to use VeriFayda 2 for new account openings. Over 5 million TIN registrations via Fayda eKYC. Cooperative Bank of Oromia enables account opening via biometric eKYC without physical documents.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Fayda integrated with Civil Registration and Residency Service Agency (CRRSA). CRRSA is a registration partner for Fayda enrollment. World Bank project explicitly supports CRVS digitalization. In 2026, Fayda ID replaces birth certificate for school registration. Integration is underway but not yet fully operationalized across all levels.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Comprehensive data sharing rules in Proclamation 1284/2023 (consent required, no third-party access without consent) and PDPP 1321/2024. Tripartite data sharing agreement signed between NIDP, RRS and UNHCR for refugee data. Relying party authorization framework defined. Data minimization principles applied.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Proclamation 1284/2023 is a dedicated Digital ID-specific law. It specifically establishes the Fayda system, NIDP institution, biometric collection rights, authentication service framework, and data protection obligations for digital identity.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 enacted and published in Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024. Comprehensive law covering consent, data minimization, purpose limitation, breach notification (72 hours), data subject rights, DPIAs, and data localization requirements.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: Ethiopian Communications Authority (ECA) designated as the data protection authority under Proclamation 1321/2024. ECA is responsible for registering data controllers/processors, issuing enforcement notices, and imposing fines. Enforcement described as nascent as of 2025 with directives still being finalized.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: Article 16(1) of Digital Identification Proclamation 1284/2023 explicitly states: 'Digital identification is legal and sufficient evidence to authenticate a person's identity.' The Fayda ID is accepted as legal proof across government and private services.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023 enacted in March 2023 provides the full legal framework. Establishes NIDP, defines enrollment rights, data protection principles, relying party rules, and criminal penalties for fraud.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: NIDP (National ID Program) is housed under the Prime Minister's Office with dedicated technical staff. MOSIP open-source platform ensures no vendor lock-in. World Bank $350M project funds capacity building and local engineer training. NIDP Executive Director emphasized building local technical ownership and avoiding black-box systems.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: NIDP is housed under the Prime Minister's Office, not the Ministry of Finance. World Bank $350M IDA financing subject to standard World Bank financial management oversight. Limited evidence of specific Ministry of Finance direct oversight of the digital ID program budget.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: Funded by $350M World Bank IDA loan/grant (Dec 2023). Government shows strong political commitment under Digital Ethiopia 2025/2030. Revenue potential from printed card fees and authentication services. MOSIP open-source reduces licensing costs. However, current heavy reliance on donor financing; long-term fiscal sustainability plan not fully documented.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: Fayda collects three biometric modalities: 10-print fingerprints, iris (both eyes), and face photograph, meeting MOSIP standards. Collection performed via Integrated Biometrics Kojak scanner supporting offline/battery-powered operation.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Fayda uses a centralized, secure electronic database with biometric deduplication (one person, one identity principle). MOSIP platform with dedicated data center infrastructure. Data localization law requires storage within Ethiopia. Biometric ABIS (Automated Biometric Identification System) operational.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Fayda is built on MOSIP open-source platform with interoperability by design. Architecture complies with W3C and EU eIDAS standards. MESOB (one-stop government portal) uses Fayda API Bridge Gateway for cross-agency data sharing. Data exchange platform integrates 91+ agencies. AU ID interoperability framework under active discussion.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: National Bank of Ethiopia mandated Fayda for all new bank account openings (Addis Ababa from Jan 2025, nationwide from Jan 2026). All existing bank accounts must be linked by March 30, 2026. VeriFayda 2 eKYC required for all banking transactions. Commercial Bank of Ethiopia, Cooperative Bank of Oromia and all NBE-regulated institutions enrolled.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: Registration and the Fayda Identification Number (FIN delivered via SMS) are free of charge. However, a physical printed ID card requires a payment fee. Digital copy accessible via telebirr super app at no cost. The basic credential (FIN number) is free; only the physical card has a fee.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: FaydaPass digital wallet launched at ID4Africa 2025 designed for cross-border use. Architecture complies with W3C and EU eIDAS interoperability standards. AU ID interoperability framework actively discussed; Ethiopia advocating for reciprocal ID recognition with African neighbors under AfCFTA. PKI system inaugurated in 2025. No formal bilateral cross-border recognition treaties yet finalized.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Formally voluntary under Proclamation 1284/2023. However, de facto mandatory for accessing key services: new bank accounts (NBE mandate Jan 2026), SIM cards (Ethio Telecom), TIN registration, passport, national exams (education), social services. Relying parties legally allowed to require Fayda with regulator approval.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: Fayda enables access to health centers as stated in UNHCR refugee ID benefits. Community-based health insurance scheme covering 55 million people targeted for Fayda integration. Health sector listed as a priority sector for Fayda mobilization. Integration with healthcare services operational in some facilities.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: All legal residents of Ethiopia are eligible regardless of nationality, including foreign nationals with valid residence permits and all registered refugees and asylum seekers aged 5+. NIDP-UNHCR-RRS tripartite agreement enables refugee inclusion. Ethiopia hosts ~1 million refugees, targeting 814,000 under GRF 2023 pledge.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: As of early 2026 approximately 29.5 million enrolled out of ~130 million population (~22.7%). By September 2025 World Bank reported 25 million+. Target is 90 million by 2027-2030. Coverage is growing rapidly with Ethio Telecom, Commercial Bank of Ethiopia and other partners.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: World Bank project includes third-party security and software code audits as a funded component. Security risk assessment and management plan required under World Bank ESMF. Academic security risk assessment proposal submitted (Naol Teshome, 2025) indicating formal government-led independent security audit not yet completed. NIDP emphasizes data security and cybersecurity awareness.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM cards are now linked to Fayda ID. Ethio Telecom (state telecom with 85 million+ subscribers) mandated to use Fayda for SIM registration. Ethio Telecom is a major Fayda registration partner issuing 3.8 million physical cards. Telecom regulator has issued directives requiring Fayda ID for SIM card issuance.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: Fayda used for safety net payments and social protection program access. Homeless and internally displaced persons (IDPs) use Fayda to access government shelter and social services. Health insurance scheme (55 million people) being integrated with Fayda. Integration with social programs underway but not yet fully universal.
